summary: Automatic gas light set up on Lehua in 1931, 18 miles west of Kauai; built to run unwatched, now a solar Coast Guard light in a seabird sanctuary.

structures.note: short concrete tower (Bulletin 1931); a solar-powered light on a fiberglass pole from 1989 (survey)

access.note: Federal property under the U.S. Coast Guard and a state seabird sanctuary managed by DLNR (2009 survey). No source here gives public access.

notes_for_editor: Height disagrees: 702 ft (Bulletin 1931, printed p. 67, and survey p. 4, which gives 213 m), 707 ft (Washington Times, May 1931), 709 ft (Bulletin 1936); the story gives all three and does not choose. Range: the Bulletin rated the light at 15 miles and gave about 20 miles in clear weather; the station record's 7 nm and Wikipedia's 9 nm are not cited. Who set the island aside: the Bulletin says the Territory's governor by executive order on 10 Aug 1928, confirmed by the President; the survey (citing Dean 1991) dates the transfer to federal control 1928. Bulletin page: printed p. 67 confirmed on the page image (PDF p. 16); PDF p. 15 is printed p. 66, a different article. The Bulletin's OCR interleaves columns, so quotes were checked against the image. The Bulletin's tender Kukui sentence is garbled in OCR and is not cited; the Kukui mention is the survey's photo caption (p. 19). Survey page numbers checked against the PDF's printed folios: PDF 9 = vii, 13 = 1, 14 = 2, 16 = 4, 24 = 12, 30 = 18, 31 = 19, 45 = 33, 46 = 34, 99 = 87. The survey's 'discontinued in 1948' sentence refers to Ka'ula, not Lehua, and is not used. The 1921 Commissioner's report calls the acetylene light 'proposed'; no source here says when it was built, so 1931 is the first lighting; the 1931 date is the survey's date of establishment. The survey says the original light and its outbuildings no longer exist; the 2025 light is the Carmanah unit. No keeper roster (USLHS roster returns none for this station). Not checked: NRHP listing, USCG Historian's light-station index, Dean 1991 (cited only as the survey cites it), LighthouseFriends. The 2025 Kauai Now report gives 'On Friday' and 'On April 11, 2025' for the same visit; the story gives only the 16 April 2025 publication date. Access: no source here says whether the island is open to visitors; the story does not encourage landing.
